pages.name: One current
pages.text: Six cells in series make a [[string]]. Each cell is drawn as a tank. Five hold 100 Ah, and one faded cell holds, say, 80 Ah. A 10 A load draws from the string. The current has only one path, through every cell. So each hour every tank gives the same 10 Ah, whatever its size. After 4 hours, the big tanks hold 60 Ah and the small one 40 Ah.

pages.name: The small cell's share
pages.task: A 10 A load runs for 4 hours. How many ampere-hours has the 80 Ah cell given?
pages.why: Series gives the current one path, so 10 A flows through every cell. In 4 hours, each cell gives 10 × 4 = 40 Ah. Size makes no difference to what flows. It only sets how long a cell lasts.

pages.name: The small cell runs out
pages.text: At 8 hours, the small tank has given its 80 Ah and is empty. The big tanks still hold 20 Ah each. Every amp must pass the empty cell to reach the load. So the string can reach that charge only by driving the empty cell backwards. The string's volts fall away here, so its useful capacity is 80 Ah, not 100.

pages.name: How long it lasts
pages.task: A string has five 100 Ah cells and one of 70 Ah. It feeds 10 A. How long does it last?
pages.why: Every cell gives 10 Ah an hour. The 70 Ah cell is empty after 70 ÷ 10 = 7 hours. Every amp must pass through it, so the string is finished then. The big cells still hold charge. The string could reach it only by driving the empty cell backwards.

pages.task: The 80 Ah cell is empty, and the load stays on. What happens to that cell?

pages.name: Full first
pages.text: Now the string charges from flat at 10 A. After 8 hours the small tank is full. The big tanks need 20 Ah more each. So the full cell turns the current into heat and gas. pages.name: After full
pages.task: Charging from flat, the small cell is full after 8 hours. What does the current do in that cell for the next 2 hours?
pages.answer: It turns into heat and gas, overcharging the cell
pages.why: The big cells need 20 Ah more each, so the charger keeps 10 A flowing. That current must pass through the full cell. It can store no more. So it turns the current into heat and gas. That is overcharge.

pages.name: Total on target
pages.task: Six cells float at 13.38 V, right on target. One cell reads 2.08 V. Is the battery healthy?
pages.answer: No: that cell is 0.15 V below 2.23 V, outside the band
pages.why: The charger holds the total at 13.38 V, whatever the cells do. So the other five rise to 2.26 V each to make up the shortfall. The band runs from 2.18 to 2.33 V. At 2.08 V, the odd cell is 0.15 V below 2.23 V, well outside it. Only cell-by-cell readings find it.

pages.name: Strings in parallel
pages.text: Two strings of 10 mΩ share a 100 A load in parallel. String A's cable is 2 mΩ and B's is 6 mΩ, so their paths are 12 and 16 mΩ. pages.name: Cable share
pages.task: Two 10 mΩ strings share 100 A, on cables of 2 and 8 mΩ. What does string A carry?
pages.why: String A's path is 10 + 2 = 12 mΩ, and B's is 10 + 8 = 18 mΩ. Each path loses the same volts, so each takes current inversely to its resistance. A carries 100 × 18 ÷ 30 = 60 A, and B carries 40 A.

pages.name: Two blocks in series
pages.task: Two 12 V blocks in series each have an emf of 12.6 V behind 7 mΩ. Together they feed 100 A. What do the terminals read?
pages.why: In series, the emfs add to 25.2 V, and the resistances add to 14 mΩ. At 100 A, 14 mΩ loses 1.4 V. So the terminals read 25.2 − 1.4 = 23.8 V.

pages.name: Series or parallel
pages.task: Do two 12 V 100 Ah blocks store more energy in series or in parallel?
pages.why: In series, the volts add to 24 V, but the ampere-hours stay at 100 Ah. In parallel, the ampere-hours add to 200 Ah, but the volts stay at 12 V. Energy is volts times ampere-hours. So both give 2400 Wh.

pages.name: Low again
pages.task: An equalise brings a low cell inside the band. Two days later it reads 0.15 V low again. What does that tell you?
pages.answer: The cell itself is faulty, so trend it and test its capacity
pages.why: A charge can cover a weak cell for a while. But a faulty cell loses its charge faster than the rest, so the fault comes back within hours. The charger is not the problem. So trend that cell's readings, and test its capacity.
